attributes.context: This appears in Article Twentieth (Piece Rates), paragraph 4, alongside rules for setting piece rates and before Article Twenty-First (Check-Off); it establishes a cooperative obligation to set piece-rate standards and, upon the Association's request, for the Union to perform engineering studies aimed at shop efficiency, modernization, and competitiveness.

extraction_text: The parties will work cooperatively to establish standards for the setting of piece rates using the good offices of available organizations including, but not limited to, T.C. Square, GIDC or CAF; and at the specific request of the Association, the Union will conduct engineering studies for the purpose of making recommendations on how to improve shop efficiency, modernization and competitiveness.

attributes.context: It appears in Article Twenty-Four: Cutting, within the conditions for an employer that may engage exclusively in the business of cutting garments as a cutting contractor.

extraction_text: The Employer may use photo-marking machines, but only on its own premises and photocopies of markers shall not be made except by cutters covered by this Agreement and who are members of Local 10.

attributes.context: The surrounding text requires the employer to maintain an efficient shop and machinery and equipment in good working condition, and workers to perform work conscientiously and efficiently.

extraction_text: New machinery may be introduced upon consent of the Union. Should the parties fail to agree, the dispute shall be subject to arbitration hereunder.

attributes.context: Paragraph 9 frames the consent requirement as part of protecting employment opportunities and preventing discrimination in work distribution between workers in inside shops of jobbers/manufacturers under a collective agreement and workers in contractor shops.

extraction_text: the Employer shall not decrease the number of machines in its factory without the consent of the Association and Local 23-25.
